fabric-api-base.reason: Shipped by Fabricated (vendored from upstream); every Fabric API module builds on it.

fabric-dimensions-v1.reason: Forge loads DataFixerUpper outside the layers Mixin transforms, so upstream's TaggedChoiceMixin and TaggedChoiceTaggedChoiceTypeMixin would never apply, and V2832Mixin, which casts DataFixerUpper's tagged choice type to the interface they add, would fail when the data fixers are built: the three are left out and the rest of the module loads. Lost: upgrading a world whose dimensions use a chunk generator type no installed mod registers fails in DataFixerUpper as it does without Fabric API (UNVERIFIED whether Forge's own handling covers it).

fabric-loot-api-v3.reason: Shipped by Fabricated: upstream's builder and drop mixins as they are, its loading hook replaced by Forge's LootTableLoadEvent (upstream's conflicts with Forge's loot loading).

fabric-object-builder-api-v1.reason: Forge keeps an attribute builder's entries in a map of its own, where upstream's accessor reads vanilla's ImmutableMap builder, so pre-flight disabled the module (and fabric-data-attachment-api-v1, which needs it). The accessor's one use, copying an entity type's default attributes for FabricDefaultAttributeRegistry.MODIFY, takes Forge's copy constructor from the in-game mod instead. Upstream runs MODIFY as the built-in registries freeze, which Forge does at bootstrap, before any Fabric mod has registered a listener: its hook is left out and the in-game mod runs MODIFY in Forge's EntityAttributeModificationEvent, after every registration and before Forge builds the attributes the game reads.

fabric-tag-api-v1.reason: Forge's tag files already have a remove list, which its tag loader applies, and upstream's FabricTagFile.remove() reads it: upstream's own list conflicts with Forge's, and its tag loader hooks, which apply that list, are left out with it. Fabricated adds fabric:remove entries to Forge's list instead (the in-game mod's TagFileRemoveMixin).
